notes: Runner clicked for credits for most of the game, reaching 28 credits and never using them. The Corp scored three remote agendas without the Runner ever contesting them.
Corp made sensible fast advances in iced remotes and set a good Urtica Cipher trap; credits briefly dropped to 0 and a few credit clicks came while already rich.
Runner never installed a single card and banked 60 credits by clicking. Its only runs were breakerless facechecks into ETR ice while the Corp scored freely.
Corp had a coherent plan with Nico Campaign economy and agendas scored behind Ansel 1.0. It made good use of Ansel installs and only a few idle credit clicks.
Runner applied good pressure on R&D and HQ and broke through a three-ice remote for the steal. The cost was a tagged facecheck into Doomscroll and some slow tag-clearing turns.
Corp left HQ flooded with agendas behind a single Tithe and spent turn 2 drawing and clicking credits instead of protecting HQ. The Runner took three agendas from HQ early.
Runner's early HQ and R&D steals were good, but it then sat on 0-4 credits for about eight turns, making mostly Archives runs. It won with a low-credit facecheck through four remote ice.
Runner installed nothing all game and clicked up 53 credits. Its two runs were breakerless facechecks while the Corp scored five agendas.

Corp used Longevity Serum to trash its whole hand, including agendas, into an unprotected Archives, which left it with no cards and 1 credit. It then installed a lightly advanced agenda that was stolen.
In a short game, Corp made a clean setup and flatlined the Runner with Saisentan on turn 2; there was too little play to judge further.
Corp kept Next Big Thing in HQ behind only a non-ETR ice after the Runner had revealed it with Burner. It spent turns piling on pointless tags instead of protecting or installing the agenda.
Runner started strongly, then repeatedly ran HQ to see known Descent and Archives into Hammer, losing programs. Broke at 0 credits, it never contested the three final remote scores.

Corp repeatedly spent its last credits trashing a cheap Stoneship Chart Room and sat at 0 credits for many turns. It installed agendas behind non-ETR ice (Paywall, Virtual Service Agent), and they were stolen.
Runner dug R&D well early but never contested the remote where the Corp kept installing and scoring agendas. Its last turns were pure credit clicks with 14-18 credits before the winning score.
Runner checked Archives for agendas well and applied good R&D pressure. It made a low-credit facecheck into Vampyronassa that paid off and ignored one naked remote install.

Corp let an Ansel install overwrite an advanced card in its remote, which sent Méliès City into an unprotected Archives. It then never iced Archives, and the Runner stole Méliès City there for the win.
After reaching 5 points the Runner sat on 0-5 credits and ran the same R&D every turn. Meanwhile the Corp scored four agendas from Server 1 uncontested.
Corp played Neurospike twice for no effect and installed Yagi-Uda behind one ice the Runner could break. It then stacked ice on an empty remote while broke and leaving R&D thin.
Corp used Ansel 1.0 on HQ to protect a hand full of agendas and scored efficiently from a remote with Seamless Launch and Wage Workers. Its early turns were a little slow.
Runner stole remote agendas efficiently but spent long stretches clicking for credits at 20-34 credits without pressuring HQ or R&D. It also declined to pay 3 credits into Grubber while holding 34.
